statement_record.book: A monotone map f : P → Q PRESERVES MEETS when f(a ∧ b) ≅ f(a) ∧ f(b) for all a, b ∈ P, and PRESERVES JOINS when f(a ∨ b) ≅ f(a) ∨ f(b); stated for binary meets/joins and only up to the preorder's induced isomorphism, not equality.
statement_record.intree: Class CartesianFunctor := { fobj_prod_iso {x y : C} : F (x × y) ≅ F x × F y; fmap_exl : fmap exl ≈ exl ∘ prod_out; fmap_exr : fmap exr ≈ exr ∘ prod_out; fmap_fork ... } — and for arbitrary shapes: Definition preserves_colimit (P : PreservesColimit G F) (L : Colimit G) : IsAColimit (F ◯ G) (F (colimit_apex L)); Class PreservesLimit := { preserves_limit (L : Limit G) : IsALimit (F ◯ G) (F L) }.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger in generality but never brought to the book's setting: the in-tree notions concern functors between arbitrary categories (the book's monotone map is the thin-category instance) and pin the comparison to the CANONICAL map via fmap_exl/fmap_exr, which is exactly what the book intends, since in a preorder an isomorphism is mutual ≤ and the canonical comparison always exists. Two mismatches to record: (a) CartesianFunctor requires the whole of C and D to be Cartesian, where Def 1.92 needs only the individual binary meets to exist; (b) the arbitrary-shape form PreservesLimit/PreservesColimit is apex-only — the IsALimit it yields carries its own cone rather than the image of the original cone — which is genuinely weaker than cone-level preservation in a general category (cf. PreservesImageLimit in Construction/Comma/Limit.v), though it coincides with the book's condition in a thin category, where 'is a meet' is a property of the object.

Program Definition Proset {A : Type} {R : relation A} (P : PreOrder R) : Category := {| obj := A; hom := R; homset := fun A B => {| Setoid.equiv := fun _ _ => True |}; id := fun x => @reflexivity A R (@PreOrder_Reflexive A R P) x; compose := fun x y z f g => @transitivity A R (@PreOrder_Transitive A R P) x y z g f |}

statement_record.book: A Galois connection between preorders P and Q is a pair of monotone maps f : P → Q and g : Q → P such that for all p ∈ P and q ∈ Q, f(p) ≤ q if and only if p ≤ g(q) (the numbered display (1.96)); f is the left adjoint, g the right adjoint.
statement_record.intree: Class Adjunction := { adj {x y} : @Isomorphism Sets {| carrier := @hom C (F x) y |} {| carrier := @hom D x (U y) |}; to_adj_nat_l ...; to_adj_nat_r ...; from_adj_nat_l ...; from_adj_nat_r ... } — over Program Definition Proset (P : PreOrder R) : Category := {| obj := A; hom := R; homset := fun A B => {| equiv := fun _ _ => True |}; id := reflexivity; compose := transitivity |}.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same in substance at thin categories, intree-stronger in general. Instantiating Adjunction at Proset P / Proset Q makes `adj` an isomorphism in Sets between the hom-setoids `f p ≤ q` and `p ≤ g q`, i.e. exactly the biconditional (1.96) in both directions; and because Proset's hom-setoid identifies all parallel proofs (equiv := fun _ _ => True), the four naturality fields hold vacuously, so nothing beyond the book's condition is demanded in the order case. For general categories the class is properly stronger than a bare bijection of hom-sets (naturality in both variables is required), which is the correct categorification rather than a mismatch.
